[§ CheatSheet for the Wiki Syntax §]

This page describes the current wiki behavior implemented by [.|js/viewer.wiki.js.] and [.|index.html.].
Those files are the authority when this quick sheet and older examples disagree.

[=Document Title Header=]

Wiki pages may start with a dedicated first line that sets the document title:

[.
|[§ My Document Name §]
.]

- this header must be the very first line in the file
- it is not rendered as page content
- if the header is missing (or empty), the viewer falls back to the file name as the document title

[=Basic Principle=]

Most syntax uses bracketed forms.
Block syntax on its own line creates its own element.
Inline syntax only affects running text.

Leading whitespace is ignored by the parser.
Indentation does not change layout and does not create nested paragraphs.

Lines without a block marker join into one paragraph.
Line breaks inside such a paragraph render like soft wraps.
An empty line ends the paragraph.

That means:

- a single source line break inside a paragraph is rendered as a space
- use an empty line if you want a visible paragraph break

Where it stays readable, this page shows examples as [.|Source.] versus [.|Rendered.] in tables so the syntax and the live result stay together.

[=Escapes=]
[| [*Source*] ][ [*Rendered*] |]
[| [.|[[[[.]  ][ [[           |]
[| [.|]]]].]  ][ ]]           |]

[=Headings=]

There is exactly one heading form:

[| [*Source*] ][ [*Rendered*] |]
[| [.|[=Title=].] ][ [.wiki|[[=Title=]].] |]

- headings start at the beginning of the line
- headings appear in the table of contents
- there is no second or third heading level; [.|[[==Title==]].] and [.|[[===Title===]].] are invalid

[=Lists=]

The block list markers are:

[| [*Source*] ][ [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.
  |- Dash marker
  |o Circle marker
  |* Dot marker
  |** Nested dot marker
  |*** Deeper nested dot marker
  |# Square marker
  |> Arrow marker
  |>> Nested arrow marker
  |>>> Deeper nested arrow marker
  .]
][
  - Dash marker
  o Circle marker
  * Dot marker
  ** Nested dot marker
  *** Deeper nested dot marker
  # Square marker
  > Arrow marker
  >> Nested arrow marker
  >>> Deeper nested arrow marker
|]

- a line without a marker continues the previous paragraph or list item, unless an empty line appears before it
- repeating the same marker increases the visual indentation depth, for example [.|**.], [.|>>>.], or [.|###.]
- list items can therefore span multiple source lines by omitting the marker on continuation lines

[=Inline Formatting=]
[| [*Feature*]    ][ [*Source*]            ][ [*Rendered*]  |]
[| underlined     ][ [.| XXX[[_YYY_]]ZZZ.] ][ XXX[_YYY_]ZZZ |]
[| struck through ][ [.| XXX[[-YYY-]]ZZZ.] ][ XXX[-YYY-]ZZZ |]
[| italic         ][ [.| XXX[[/YYY/]]ZZZ.] ][ XXX[/YYY/]ZZZ |]
[| bold           ][ [.| XXX[[*YYY*]]ZZZ.] ][ XXX[*YYY*]ZZZ |]
[| red            ][ [.| XXX[[!YYY!]]ZZZ.] ][ XXX[!YYY!]ZZZ |]
[| superscript    ][ [.| XXX[['YYY']]ZZZ.] ][ XXX['YYY']ZZZ |]
[| subscript      ][ [.| XXX[[,YYY,]]ZZZ.] ][ XXX[,YYY,]ZZZ |]

- inline markers may be nested if they close correctly

[=Links=]

Normal wiki links use the less-than form:

[| [*Source*]                                 ][ [*Rendered*]                          |]
[| [.|[<TODO.wiki|TODO File>].]               ][ [<TODO.wiki|TODO File>]               |]
[| [.|[<https://example.com|External Link>].] ][ [<https://example.com|External Link>] |]

Important rules:

- a target without an extension is treated as a wiki page and gets [.|.wiki.] implicitly
- [.|.wiki.], [.|.spo.], [.|.ilt.], [.|.mermaid.], and [.|.mmd.] open in repo viewers
- explicit targets with other extensions resolve as files or assets
- raw URLs, [.|www.example.com.], and mail addresses are auto-linked
- the legacy board-link form [.|[[?Title?]].] is still recognized

[| [*Source*] ][ [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.
  |This is a paragraph.
  |This line still belongs to it.
  .]
][

  This line still belongs to it.
|]
[|

  |
  |Second paragraph.
  .]
][

  Second paragraph.
|]
[|

  .]
][

|]
[|
  [.
  |[| [*Name*] ][ [*Value*] |]
  |[| Alpha    ][ 1         |]
  |[| A | B    ][ 2         |]
  .]
][
  [| [*Name*] ][ [*Value*] |]
  [| Alpha    ][ 1         |]
  [| A | B    ][ 2         |]
|]

[=External Resource Blocks=]

Hash blocks reference files or URLs:

[| [*Source*] ][ [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.
  |[#
  ||../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO
  |#]
  .]
][
  [#
  |../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO
  #]
|]

- paths are relative to the current wiki file
- [.|.wiki.], [.|.spo.], [.|.ilt.], [.|.mermaid.], and [.|.mmd.] use viewers
- images and videos use built-in media rendering
- plain text files without a dedicated viewer fall back to code-style rendering

[=Embedded Resource Blocks=]

Embedded resource blocks store the content directly in the wiki file.
Use them when the resource should render as its own block instead of referencing an external file.

Pattern:

[.
|[.extension
||content
|.]
.]

- the opening line starts with the extension and stays open until the standalone closing line
- the extension selects the viewer and also decides whether the content is treated as text or binary
- for text resources, a leading helper pipe on each content line is stripped
- for binary resources, write Base64 between the opening and closing lines
- this multiline form is different from the inline compact form [.|[[.kind|value.]].]

Examples:

[| [*Source*] ][ [*Rendered*] |]
[|
  [.
  |[.
  ||first line
  ||second line
  |.]
  .]
][
  [.
  |first line
  |second line
  .]
|]
[|
  [.
  |[.spo
  ||§VAR X := 1
  ||§EXPORT X
  |.]
  .]
][
  [.spo
  |§VAR X := 1
  |§EXPORT X
  .]
|]
[|
  [.
  |[.mermaid
  ||graph LR
  ||    A[Square Rect] -- Link text --> B((Circle))
  ||    A --> C(Round Rect)
  ||    B --> D{Rhombus}
  ||    C --> D  |.]
  .]
][
  [.mermaid
  |graph LR
  |    A[Square Rect] -- Link text --> B((Circle))
  |    A --> C(Round Rect)
  |    B --> D{Rhombus}
  |    C --> D
  .]
|]

[=Inline Objects=]

Use inline objects inside running text or inside table cells.

There are two inline forms:

- [.|[[# target #]].] uses the same hash syntax as the block form above, but inside a paragraph it renders inline
- [.|[[.kind|value.]].] renders a compact code or resource chip
- inside [.|[[.kind|value.]].], write [.|.]].] in the source when the value itself must contain [.|.]].]
- inline hash objects can also show inline previews for images
- if you want full block rendering, use a standalone hash block or the multiline embedded-resource form instead

[| [*Source*]                                                             ][ [*Rendered*]                                                     |]
[| [.|See [[# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #]] inline.] ][ See [# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #] inline. |]
[| [.|Use [[.|first line.]] inline.]                                      ][ Use [.|first line.] inline.                                   |]

[=Viewers By Extension=]

There are dedicated viewers for:

- [.|.wiki.]
- [.|.spo.] and [.|.ilt.]
- [.|.mermaid.] and [.|.mmd.]

The supported image file formats:

- binary: [.|.avif.], [.|.bmp.], [.|.gif.], [.|.ico.], [.|.jpeg.], [.|.jpg.], [.|.png.], [.|.webp.]
- text based: [.|.svg.]

[=EBNF=]

[.
|(* Escaping
|
|In normal text and restricted content:
|
|	[[  means literal [
|	]]  means literal ]
|
|For close tokens ending in ], closing is decided right-to-left.
|A close token is real only if the number of immediately following ] characters is even.
|If the number is odd, one ] escapes the close token and the close token is emitted literally.
|
|Example for close token #]:
|
|	[#abc#]    closes
|	[#abc#]]   emits literal #]
|	[#abc#]]]  closes, followed by escaped/literal ] depending on context
|*)
|
|
|document        = [ "[§" , restrictedContent , "§]" , [ emptyLine ] ] ,
|                  { emptyLine | block } ;
|
|
|block           = heading
|                | "[---]"                                              (* horizontal rule *)
|
|                | table
|
|                | "[\"" , newline ,
|                    { whitespace , "|" , text , newline } ,
|                  "\"]"                                              (* quote block *)
|
|                | "[#"  , newline ,
|                    { whitespace , "|" , text , newline } ,
|                  "#]"                                                (* resource / metadata block *)
|
|                | "[." , extension , newline ,
|                    { whitespace , "|" , text , newline } ,
|                  ".]"                                                (* extension-defined block *)
|
|                | list
|                | paragraph ;
|
|
|heading         = "[=" , restrictedContent , "=]" ;                 (* section heading *)
|
|
|table           = { lineTableRow | blockTableRow } ;
|
|
|lineTableRow    = "[|" ,
|                    inlineText ,
|                    { " ][ " , inlineText } ,
|                  "|]" ;
|
|
|blockTableRow   = "[|" , newline ,
|                    document ,
|                    { "][" , newline , document } ,
|                  "|]" ;
|
|
|list            = { listItem } ;
|
|
|listItem        = ( "-" , { "-" }                                  (* dash list *)
|                  | "o" , { "o" }                                  (* circle list *)
|                  | "*" , { "*" }                                  (* filled bullet list *)
|                  | "#" , { "#" }                                  (* square list *)
|                  | ">" , { ">" } )                                (* arrow list *)
|
|                  , whitespace ,
|                  inlineText ,
|                  { continuationLine } ;
|
|
|continuationLine = inlineText
|                   (* stops at empty line, new list marker, or block start *) ;
|
|
|paragraph       = inlineText , { inlineText } ;
|
|
|inlineText      = { inlineToken
|                  | textChar
|                  | "[["                                              (* literal [ *)
|                  | "]]"                                              (* literal ] *)
|                  | "[---]" } ;                                       (* inline horizontal rule *)
|
|
|inlineToken     = "[*" , inlineText , "*]"                          (* strong / bold *)
|                | "[/" , inlineText , "/]"                          (* emphasis / italic *)
|                | "[_" , inlineText , "_]"                          (* underline *)
|                | "[-" , inlineText , "-]"                          (* deleted / strike-through *)
|                | "[!" , inlineText , "!]"                          (* alert / highlighted span *)
|                | "[(" , inlineText , ")]"                          (* small text *)
|                | "['" , inlineText , "']"                          (* superscript *)
|                | "[," , inlineText , ",]"                          (* subscript *)
|
|                | "[\"" , restrictedContent , "\"]"               (* inline quote *)
|                | "[#" , restrictedContent , "#]"                   (* resource reference *)
|
|                | "[<" ,
|                    restrictedContent ,
|                    [ "|" , linkLabel ] ,
|                  ">]"                                                (* link: target | optional label *)
|
|                | "[." ,
|                    extension ,
|                    "|" ,
|                    opaqueContent ,
|                  ".]" ;                                              (* inline embed handled by extension viewer *)
|
|
|restrictedContent = { restrictedChar | "[[" | "]]" } ;
|
|
|opaqueContent   = { anyChar | "[[" | "]]" } ;
|
|
|extension       = extensionChar , { extensionChar } ;
|
|
|extensionChar   = ? any non-whitespace char except "[" , "]" , "|" ? ;
|restrictedChar  = ? any char except raw "[" and raw "]" unless escaped ? ;
|textChar        = ? any char except raw "[" and raw "]" ? ;
|
|
|emptyLine       = whitespace ;
|whitespace      = { " " | "\t" } ;
|newline         = "\n" ;
.]
